common_name: Rose Supreme Gladiolus (Peachy-Salmon Ruffled Tall Gladiolus)

planting.note: Plant corms 4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed, and stagger plantings every two weeks for a longer bloom season. Rose Supreme bears peachy-salmon flowers with ruffled edges on tall 3-4 foot spikes.

directions: Rose Supreme bears soft, peachy-salmon flowers with gently ruffled petal edges on tall, sturdy 3 to 4 foot spikes, a warm, sunset-toned color valued by cut-flower growers for its versatility in mixed bouquets. Plant corms in well-drained soil and stake or plant in blocks to support the tall flower spikes, which open from the bottom up over several weeks. Cut spikes for indoor arrangements once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm. In colder zones, lift and store corms after foliage yellows in fall.

planting.note: Plant corms 4 inches deep in full sun after the danger of frost has passed; Boone is a cold-hardy Gladiolus dalenii species hybrid with peachy-apricot flowers, yellow centers, and red-streaked throats, hardier than most hybrid gladiolus.

directions: Boone, a Gladiolus dalenii species hybrid, bears warm peachy-apricot flowers with yellow centers and red-streaked throats, and unlike most modern hybrid gladiolus, it tolerates significantly colder winters, often surviving in the ground through zone 6 winters where standard gladiolus corms must be lifted and stored. Plant corms in well-drained soil in full sun, and let clumps remain in place over winter in zones where it is hardy rather than digging annually. Cut spikes for indoor arrangements once the lowest two or three florets show color, leaving at least four leaves on the plant to recharge the corm.
